title: Classical and quantum spectral density estimation under local graph access
authors: Rong-Hua Li, Meihao Liao, Yichun Yang
abstract: We study spectral density estimation for the normalized adjacency matrix of an unweighted graph under local access model. Previously, Cohen-Steiner et al. [KDD 2018] proposed an algorithm for $\varepsilon$-approximate spectral density estimation in the Wasserstein-1 distance, using $2^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$ local queries to the graph. In this paper, we prove that every constant-success estimator with Wasserstein--$1$ error at most $\eps$ requires $2^{Ω(1/\eps)}$ queries, showing that the Cohen-Steiner algorithm is optimal up to constant in the exponent. This resolves the open problem left by previous researches Jin et al. [COLT 2023] and Peng et al. [COLT 2026].   We then turn to quantum local access model. We give an $\widetilde O(\eps^{-3})$-query algorithm estimating the spectral density with Wasserstein-1 error at most $\eps$. Finally, we prove a $\widetildeΩ(\eps^{-4/3})$ quantum lower bound when the graph is sufficiently large. As a result, quantum local access model changes the dependence on $\eps$ from exponential to polynomial.
summary: This paper analyzes spectral density estimation for graphs under limited local access, comparing classical and quantum query complexity. It proves that while the classical model requires an exponentially large number of queries, the quantum model achieves a polynomial scaling, demonstrating a clear quantum advantage. This advances the understanding of quantum query complexity in graph signal processing.
main_problem: The paper addresses the problem of estimating the spectral density of a graph's normalized adjacency matrix under limited local access to the graph structure.
main_result: It demonstrates a quantum advantage by showing that the quantum query complexity for this estimation scales polynomially ($\Omega(\epsilon^{-4/3})$) with the error $\epsilon$, significantly better than the exponential lower bound ($\Omega(2^{1/\epsilon})$) established for the classical local access model.
method: The authors combine spectral graph theory with advanced quantum query complexity techniques, utilizing tools from coding theory (self-dual codes, Lagrangians) to establish lower bounds for quantum bit oracles, which are then mapped to graph queries.
model_or_system: The system is an unweighted graph $G$, and the object of study is its normalized adjacency matrix $\mathbf{N}_G$. The analysis is framed within the quantum local access model, where graph functions are queried via reversible XOR oracles.

important_parameters: The approximation error $\epsilon$ is the key parameter, determining the scaling of the required number of queries.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the classical lower bound for spectral density estimation. It then develops the mathematical machinery using quadratic forms and self-dual codes to prove a quantum query lower bound, culminating in the comparison showing the quantum advantage.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete example where quantum computation offers a significant, provable speedup over classical algorithms for a problem rooted in graph spectral analysis, which is highly relevant to quantum algorithms for physical systems.
